$comment: Rig contract for the PRODUCTION CAGE character, lion/cage/lion.glb.
WHY A SECOND CONTRACT. lionRigContract.json describes the PROXY's
skeleton. The two rigs name the same anatomy differently -
front_shoulder_L against scapula_FL, front_lower_L against forearm_FL,
neck against neck_01 - so only 11 of its 45 bones matched the cage and
the cage could not be validated at all. Repointing the proxy's contract
would have invalidated the character that currently ships to make the
one that does not pass; renaming the cage rig would have to rewrite the
authored ring-to-bone skin map in lion_skeleton.py, which is looked up
BY NAME and would land weights on the wrong bone if a rename were
inexact. So each asset is validated on its own terms until the proxy
retires, at which point the cage's naming becomes the only naming.
GENERATED FROM INTENT, NOT FROM THE ARTIFACT. `bones` is
lion_skeleton.skeleton() - the authored table the rig is built from -
not a scrape of the exported GLB. A contract read back off its own
output can never fail.
maxBytes is 6 MB, not 4. The cage ships Catmull-Clark subdivided (L2,
999 -> 15,954 verts) because a 1,000-vert deformation cage rendered raw is
visibly faceted, and glTF has no subdivision so it must be baked. The cost
is not the geometry but the morph deltas: every one of the 16 targets stores
a delta per vertex, which is ~3.1 MB on its own. The brief's ceiling is
10 MB, so 6 leaves headroom while still catching a runaway.
All 13 clips are now REQUIRED. They were plannedClips until 2026-09-03, when
the eleven missing ones were authored. Promoting them means the contract now
fails if any regresses, which is the point of having listed them.
